A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete 20-page versions of Generative Human Geometry Distribution, with readable text, equations, tables and figures. All six appendix pages are visually identical.

before.justification: v4 reports original geometry-generation experiments, ablations, numerical comparisons in Tables 2–5, and a 25-participant user study.

after.justification: v5 retains the original experiments, quantitative results, user study and qualitative appendix results.

M1.justification: Sections 4.2–4.4 retain the same training-pair construction, distribution normalization, feature-map auto-decoder and conditional generation procedures. No method component changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use THuman2 for pose-conditioned generation and 4DDress for novel-pose generation. The appendix scenarios involving loose clothing, body-shape variation and identity interpolation are also unchanged.

E2.justification: Tables 2–5 and the qualitative comparisons retain the same comparators, including VecSet, ENARF, GNARF, EVA3D, E3Gen, GetAvatar and gDNA in their respective experiments. The two newly cited works are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Evaluation settings remain identical, including 10,000/30,000-iteration formulation comparisons, 25,000 rendered normal images for FID, and the user study with 2 identities, 8 poses and 25 participants.

E4.justification: The training-pair and architecture ablations, convergence analyses, incompatible-feature-map examples, body-shape variations and latent interpolations are retained unchanged in Sections 5 and 9.

E5.justification: Neither version adds repeated-run or seed information, confidence intervals, error bars or formal significance tests. The existing point-estimate reporting remains unchanged.

E6.justification: Numerical and qualitative results are unchanged throughout. For example, Table 4 retains raw-geometry FID values of 42.90 for gDNA and 16.16 for Ours; Table 5 retains Ours scores of 4.04 for quality and 4.36 for plausibility.

T1.justification: The geometry-distribution definitions, flow-matching formulation and objectives in Equations 1–6 are unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same novelty, high-fidelity generation, pose-awareness and performance claims, including the stated 57% geometry-quality improvement.

C2.justification: Interpretations of convergence, pose consistency and representation capability are unchanged. Section 6 retains the same limitations concerning nonuniform sampling, unseen clothing styles and UV seams.

D1.justification: Appendix 9.1 retains identical architecture, sampling counts, optimization settings, hardware, training durations and inference timings. No technical or code/data-access disclosure is added or removed.

R1.justification: Section 2.1 adds PointFlow (Yang et al., 2019) and Learning Gradient Fields for Shape Generation (Cai et al., 2020), with corresponding references. It acknowledges their conceptually similar distribution-of-distributions approach and describes their coarse shapes as distinct from the paper's high-fidelity objective.

P1.justification: A short related-work passage and two bibliography entries are added, and the arXiv version/date stamp changes. Existing prose and section order otherwise remain unchanged; shifted passages are retained content.

P2.justification: The added text causes limited layout changes, including moving Table 5 from page 8 to page 9 and shifting other displays vertically. Figure content, table structures and captions remain unchanged, as does the entire appendix layout.

improvement.justification: v5 makes the research context more complete by acknowledging two conceptually close predecessors omitted from v4 and explaining the intended high-fidelity distinction in Section 2.1. This is a limited improvement: the scientific evidence is unchanged, and the broad novelty wording in the introduction and conclusion remains unrevised.
